title: Vendor Debugging Key Swap & Escrow Playbook (Draft)
body:
Purpose and scope:

This playbook defines an operational and contractual template for granting vendors temporary cryptographic key access or key-swap privileges strictly for debugging, emergency remediation, or legally compelled disclosure, and the associated escrow and audit controls required by Redwood Inference. It is intended for use with: Private Deployments (VPC/on-prem), Dedicated-hosted integrations where customer-managed keys or HSMs are involved, and any third-party maintenance arrangements.

Notes to reviewers (internal):
- Draft is intentionally prescriptive on technical controls (HSM, split-knowledge) to reduce negotiation cycles.
- Assume customer-managed KEKs where feasible; where not possible, this template includes compensating controls.
- TODO: map to SOC2 control families and legal DPA clause numbers.

Definitions (short):
- "Temporary Key Access": short-lived, auditable privilege to unwrap or use an encryption key for a specific support activity.
- "Key Swap": replacing an active key with a new key material, typically for debugging or rotation during an incident.
- "Escrow Agent": an independent custodian (internal or third-party) holding a sealed copy or split shares of key material under documented release conditions.
- "Approval Authority": cross-functional approver set (Security + Product + Customer Representative or CRO).

High-level policy principles:
1) Principle of Least Privilege: access only to the minimum key material and for the minimum time required.
2) Auditor-in-the-loop: every temporary access instance must produce immutable evidence (signed request, approval record, timestamped logs, exported audit bundle).
3) Split custody where risk is elevated: escrow shares held across two independent custodians (e.g., Redwood HSM + neutral third party).
4) Customer control preference: default to customer-managed keys; if vendor access is required, prefer remote attested environments and ephemeral wrapping keys.

Procedural steps (operational playbook):
A. Initiation (requestor):
  - Create a support case referencing the customer, product, and affected resource. Attach technical justification and duration estimate.
  - Use the standard "Temporary Key Access Request" form (see Exhibit A). Required fields: customer contract id, targeted key id, purpose, start/end time window, rollback plan, contact list.

B. Preliminary Triage (SRE/Product):
  - Validate that debugging cannot be completed without key access. Provide certificate/attestation that alternatives (sanitized traces, mock keys, replay in staging) were attempted.
  - If request is routine (non-prod) vs emergency (prod incident), mark priority and follow corresponding escalation timelines.

C. Approvals (Approval Authority):
  - Security must approve all temporary key access requests. For production or PA/PII workloads, require an additional customer representative sign-off where contractually mandated.
  - Approvals must be recorded on-chain in the audit system (immutable record). Approvers: Security Lead (mandatory), Product Owner (mandatory), Legal (for subpoenas), Customer Security Contact (if required).

D. Technical Safeguards (execution):
  - Prefer remote execution: vendor provides signed code or approved playbook executed within a Redwood-managed attested HSM or isolated debug cluster. No plaintext key material should leave the hardware boundary.
  - If key material must be unwrapped, do so using a temporary wrapping key generated for the session; the wrapping key must be generated in an HSM and destroyed after the session with proof of destruction.
  - Split-key escrow: if escrow is used, store shares with (1) Redwood HSM module and (2) independent escrow vendor or internal legal custodian. Use Shamir's Secret Sharing with threshold = 2 of 2 for high-risk keys; consider 2-of-3 for contingency.
  - Time-boxed tokens: grant ephemeral credentials scoped to the smallest necessary API surface; tokens expire automatically at end_time.

E. Telemetry and Evidence Collection:
  - Enable debug-level telemetry for the session (only for affected process). Sample telemetry policy: sample rate <= 1% by default; increase with approval for live debugging but redact secrets.
  - Generate an Audit Bundle that includes: signed request, approvals, HSM attestation (PCR values), session transcripts, command list executed, and a hash manifest of any exported artifacts. Bundle must be sealed and stored in the secure evidence store for the retention period.

F. Post-action review and key hygiene:
  - Conduct a post-mortem within 72 hours of session completion. Document root cause, whether access was necessary, and any control gaps.
  - Rotate any keys accessed/unwrapped unless a documented risk assessment justifies retention. Rotation schedule for keys used in a session: immediate rotation + replace with new material and update all consumers.

G. Deprovisioning and proof of destruction:
  - All ephemeral credentials must be revoked immediately after session.
  - Where a wrapping key was used, produce evidence of secure destruction (HSM audit record).

Escrow-specific contractual language (template snippets for DPA/Service Agreement):
- Purpose-limited Escrow: "Provider may deposit encrypted key shares with an Escrow Agent solely for the limited purposes of emergency debugging or legal compliance. Release of escrowed material requires Approval Authority consent and a documented access request in accordance with the Provider's Temporary Key Access Procedure."
- Audit & Notice: "Provider shall provide Customer with prior notice of any planned Escrow access where feasible; in emergency incidents Provider will notify Customer within 24 hours of access and provide the Audit Bundle within 5 business days."
- Liability carve-outs: "Use of Escrow does not expand Provider's rights to access Customer data outside the scope of the approved request. Misuse of Escrowed material shall be treated as a material breach subject to indemnities in Section X."

Subpoenas and legal compulsion handling:
- Route all legal process to Legal immediately. No key material released absent Legal + Security review and an executed court order or equivalent. When compelled, preserve chain of custody and include a redaction assessment for extraneous customer data.

Minimum technical requirements checklist (for ops):
  - HSM-backed wrapping and attestation supported (Y/N).
  - Ephemeral session tokens with auto-expiration (Y/N).
  - Audit Bundle generation and secure storage (Y/N).
  - Split-escrow storage configured (Y/N).
  - Consent/notification flow with customer security contact (configured / not configured).

Exhibit A: Temporary Key Access Request (sample fields)
  - Request ID:
  - Requestor name + team:
  - Customer name / contract ID:
  - Targeted key identifier (key fingerprint):
  - Environment (prod/staging/dev):
  - Justification (plain text):
  - Risk mitigations attempted prior to request:
  - Proposed start / end window (UTC):
  - Rollback / failback plan:
  - Approvers required list:

Exhibit B: Audit Bundle Checklist
  - Signed request PDF
  - Approval log with approver signatures and timestamps
  - HSM attestation/cert chain (signed)
  - Session transcript (obfuscated)
  - List of commands and parameters executed
  - Hash manifest of any ephemeral files exported
  - Evidence of wrapping key destruction (if applicable)

Operational playbook (quick runbook for SREs):
1) Receive request -> validate with Product -> open secure ephemeral session
2) Confirm HSM boundary and generate wrapping key
3) Execute minimal unwrapping required for debugging
4) Collect audit artifacts live; do not copy keys into standard logs
5) Close session and revoke tokens
6) Trigger rotation and post-mortem

Sample internal email template (to customer security contact):
Subject: Temporary Key Access Request for {Customer} — {Request ID}
Body:
Hi {Name},

We have an approved request to perform a time-boxed key access session to remediate {issue summary}. The session window is {start} to {end} UTC. We will execute in an attested HSM and provide the Audit Bundle within 5 business days post-session. Please reply if you object or require additional controls.

Regards,
{SRE oncall}

Open questions and negotiable items for legal review (notes):
- Escrow agent selection: internal vs third-party — risk/price tradeoffs.
- Evidence retention period: default 3 years vs customer-specific requests.
- Thresholds for split-knowledge (2-of-2 vs 2-of-3) depending on contract value.

Reference materials & mapping:
- Link to existing DPA clauses: CONF-SEC-2345 (see linked_artifacts)
- HSM attestation standard we use: internal spec (link in Confluence)
